rationale:
The supplied proof of cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support combines two separate and reusable mathematical obligations. Each is now a named child; the parent keeps steps 1, 5 and 6, which are short.

(i) Locality of mass (steps 2–3). If spt(S − T) ⊆ K, then M_G(S) = M_G(T) for every G with G ∩ K = ∅. This is a pure current-level fact and needs neither integer multiplicity nor U open. The parent applies it only to open G ⊆ O = U ∖ K, but the same argument works for any such G. It is the parent's only use of vanish_off_support, and the same comparison appears wherever a competitor S differs from T only inside K.

(ii) Localized uniqueness of measures (step 4). Take Borel measures μ, ν on ℝ^P with μ finite on compact subsets of an open O and μ(G) = ν(G) for every open G ⊆ O. Then μ = ν on every Borel subset of O. This is pure measure theory, independent of currents, and the heaviest Lean step (exhaustion, π–λ uniqueness for finite measures, continuity from below). The pinned Mathlib has only the general tools ext_of_generate_finite, isPiSystem_isOpen and ext_of_generateFrom_of_cover, and no localized version. No DAG node, project file or SimonGMT file states it.

The third child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support with its byte-identical frozen type, because child (i) depends on it. The runtime maps a reused accepted name to the existing node, creates no new node and skips handoff installation for it.

- Steps 2–3: O = U ∖ K is open because K is compact, hence closed. For open G ⊆ O, G is disjoint from K, so child (i) and step 1 give μ_S(G) = μ_T(G).
- Step 4: child (ii) with μ = μ_S, ν = μ_T gives agreement on Borel subsets of O.
- Step 5: W' ∖ W ⊆ O, because W' ⊆ closure W' ⊆ U and K ⊆ W.
- Step 6: μ_T(W') = μ_T(W) + μ_T(W' ∖ W) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_S(W').

subproblems.title: A current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reuse of the accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n: a sequentially continuous linear functional on the space 𝒟ⁿ(U) of smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The support of S is spt S = U ∖ Z_S, where Z_S is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11, as formalized by GeometricCurrentOn.support). If tsupport ω ∩ spt S = ∅, then S(ω) = 0. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 2.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–301) and the standard partition-of-unity argument; Simon uses this property tacitly (e.g. in 2.12). Write 𝒲 for the family of open sets W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S vanishing on W (S(η) = 0 whenever η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport η ⊆ W); thus Z_S = ⋃𝒲 and spt S = U ∖ Z_S.
1. Since ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω is smooth with compact support, so C := tsupport ω is compact, and C ⊆ U. If C = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume C ≠ ∅.
2. From C ⊆ U and C ∩ (U ∖ Z_S) = ∅ we get C ⊆ Z_S = ⋃𝒲. The members of 𝒲 are open and C is compact, so there are W_1, …, W_N ∈ 𝒲 with C ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_N.
3. Choose a smooth partition of unity on the compact (hence closed) set C subordinate to the open cover (W_i)_{i≤N}: C^∞ functions χ_1, …, χ_N : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport χ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_{i=1}^N χ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C. (Such partitions exist on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, e.g. Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), or directly from smooth bump functions, Mathlib exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset.)
4. For each i put ω_i := χ_i ω, i.e. ω_i(x) = χ_i(x)·ω(x). Then ω_i is smooth and tsupport ω_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ C. Hence tsupport ω_i is compact and contained in U, so ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and tsupport ω_i ⊆ W_i with W_i ∈ 𝒲, so S(ω_i) = 0.
5. Σ_{i=1}^N ω_i = ω pointwise: for x ∈ C, Σ_i χ_i(x)ω(x) = ω(x); for x ∉ C, ω(x) = 0 and hence ω_i(x) = 0 for all i. By linearity of S on 𝒟ⁿ(U), S(ω) = Σ_{i=1}^N S(ω_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U missing spt S = U ∖ Z_S, so finitely many open W_i (closure compact in U) on which S vanishes cover it.
A smooth partition of unity χ_i on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i splits ω = Σ χ_i ω, each χ_i ω a test form in U supported in W_i.
S(χ_i ω) = 0 for each i, hence S(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Masses of S and T agree on every set disjoint from a set containing spt(S − T)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n), and let K, G ⊆ ℝ^P be sets with spt(S − T) ⊆ K and G ∩ K = ∅. Here S − T is the difference current of the frozen contract, (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); spt R = U ∖ Z_R is the support of a current R ∈ 𝒟_n(U), where Z_R is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and R(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support, Simon Ch. 6, 2.11); and for a current R ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and a set G, M_G(R) := sup{max(R(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors, Simon 6.2.5). Then M_G(S) = M_G(T).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (K G : Set (Euclid P)), (S - T).support ⊆ K → Disjoint G K → S.massOn G = T.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the supplied proof of the parent node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.minimality_localizes-a1 (cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support), where the argument is applied to open sets G ⊆ O = U ∖ K; it uses only G ∩ K = ∅, so it is stated here for every such G. Write 𝒜_G := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} (SimonGMT massAdmissibleOn U n G); this set depends only on U, n and G, not on the current.
1. By definition, M_G(S) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of the set {max(S(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒜_G}, and M_G(T) is the supremum of {max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒜_G}. Both suprema are taken over the same index set 𝒜_G, so it suffices to show S(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒜_G.
2. Let ω ∈ 𝒜_G. Then tsupport ω ⊆ G, and spt(S − T) ⊆ K by hypothesis. Since G ∩ K = ∅, tsupport ω ∩ spt(S − T) ⊆ G ∩ K = ∅.
3. S − T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is a current in U and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport disjoint from spt(S − T). By the sibling lemma vanish_off_support, applied to the current S − T and the form ω, (S − T)(ω) = 0. By the definition of the difference current, (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω); hence S(ω) = T(ω).
4. By steps 2–3, the functions ω ↦ max(S(ω), 0) and ω ↦ max(T(ω), 0) coincide on 𝒜_G. Therefore the two sets in step 1 are equal, and so are their suprema: M_G(S) = M_G(T). ∎
proof_key_steps: M_G(S) and M_G(T) are the suprema of max(S(ω), 0) and max(T(ω), 0) over the same admissible set 𝒜_G of test forms in 𝒟ⁿ(U) supported in G with |ω| ≤ 1.
For ω ∈ 𝒜_G, tsupport ω ⊆ G misses K ⊇ spt(S − T), so vanish_off_support applied to S − T gives (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω) = 0.
The two functions agree on 𝒜_G, so their images and suprema agree: M_G(S) = M_G(T).

subproblems.title: Measures that agree on the open subsets of an open set O, one of them finite on compact subsets of O, agree on all Borel subsets of O
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let μ, ν be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure (Euclid P)). Assume that μ(C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ O, and that μ(G) = ν(G) for every open G ⊆ O. Then μ(A) = ν(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ O.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ O → μ C ≠ ∞) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ O → μ G = ν G) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ O → μ A = ν A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of the parent node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.minimality_localizes-a1 (cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support), stated for general measures; there μ = μ_S, ν = μ_T and O = U ∖ K, and the finiteness of ν on the exhausting sets, which the parent takes from local integrability, follows here from μ(O_i) = ν(O_i). Write d(x) := inf{|x − y| : y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ O} ∈ [0, ∞] for the distance from x to ℝ^P ∖ O, with d(x) := +∞ for every x when O = ℝ^P (the infimum over the empty set). d is continuous as a map to [0, ∞] (it is 1-Lipschitz when ℝ^P ∖ O ≠ ∅ and constant otherwise), and d(x) = 0 for every x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ O.
1. (Exhaustion.) For i ∈ ℕ put O_i := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| < i and d(x) > 1/(i+1)}. (a) Each O_i is open: it is the intersection of the sets {|x| < i} and {d(x) > 1/(i+1)}, which are open by continuity of |·| and of d. (b) The set F_i := {x : |x| ≤ i and d(x) ≥ 1/(i+1)} is closed and contains O_i, so closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i. If x ∉ O, then d(x) = 0 < 1/(i+1), so x ∉ F_i; hence closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i ⊆ O. (c) closure(O_i) is closed and contained in the closed ball of radius i about 0, hence compact (Heine–Borel). (d) O_i ⊆ O_j whenever i ≤ j, since then |x| < i ≤ j and 1/(j+1) ≤ 1/(i+1). (e) ⋃_i O_i = O. Indeed O_i ⊆ closure(O_i) ⊆ O for every i. Conversely let x ∈ O. The set ℝ^P ∖ O is closed and does not contain x, so x is not in its closure and d(x) > 0. Choose an integer m ≥ 1 with 1/m < d(x) and an integer k > |x|, and put i := max(m, k). Then |x| < k ≤ i and 1/(i+1) < 1/m < d(x), so x ∈ O_i.
2. (Finiteness.) For each i, μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure(O_i)) < ∞ by hypothesis, because closure(O_i) is a compact subset of O by step 1(b),(c). Since O_i is an open subset of O, ν(O_i) = μ(O_i) < ∞.
3. (Uniqueness on O_i.) Fix i and let μ_i := μ⌞O_i and ν_i := ν⌞O_i be the restricted measures, μ_i(B) = μ(B ∩ O_i) and ν_i(B) = ν(B ∩ O_i) for Borel B. By step 2 they are finite measures. For every open G ⊆ ℝ^P, the set G ∩ O_i is open and contained in O, so μ_i(G) = μ(G ∩ O_i) = ν(G ∩ O_i) = ν_i(G); in particular μ_i(ℝ^P) = ν_i(ℝ^P) (take G = ℝ^P). The family of open subsets of ℝ^P is closed under finite intersections (a π-system) and generates the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P. Two finite measures that have the same total mass and agree on a π-system generating the σ-algebra are equal (Dynkin's π–λ uniqueness theorem; Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite with isPiSystem_isOpen). Hence μ_i = ν_i.
4. (Continuity from below.) Let A ⊆ O be a Borel set. The sets A ∩ O_i increase with i by step 1(d), and ⋃_i (A ∩ O_i) = A ∩ ⋃_i O_i = A ∩ O = A by step 1(e). By continuity of measures from below, μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i μ_i(A) and ν(A) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν_i(A). By step 3, μ_i(A) = ν_i(A) for every i; therefore μ(A) = ν(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust O by open sets O_i = {|x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 1/(i+1)} increasing to O, whose closures are compact subsets of O.
μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure O_i) < ∞ and ν(O_i) = μ(O_i), so μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i are finite measures.
μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i agree on every open G (G ∩ O_i is an open subset of O), including ℝ^P; open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so μ⌞O_i = ν⌞O_i.
For Borel A ⊆ O, continuity from below along A ∩ O_i ↑ A gives μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = ν(A).
